Key audit requirements summarized by Verdigris SIEM team:
- Primary export: Splunk HEC (preferred) + S3 archive (immutable, versioned) for long-term retention
- Acceptable transports: HTTPS (HEC), syslog over TLS, Kafka with TLS/SASL for streaming ingestion
- Log format: newline-delimited JSON, follow ECS-like field naming for compatibility; provide a manifest and field map

- Required fields in every event: timestamp_iso8601, request_id, tenant_id (pseudonymized if needed), api_path, model_name, model_version, action (generate|embed|rerank), input_token_count, output_token_count, latency_ms, response_size_bytes, kv_cache_hit (true|false), routing_decision, fallback_reason (nullable), http_status, error_code (nullable), region, host_instance_id
- Access logs: admin UI logins, API key usage, token creation/deletion, role changes. Must include actor_id, actor_role, ip_address (anonymized as CIDR or hashed if required by privacy), timestamp
- Key usage logs: KMS key_id, operation (Encrypt|Decrypt|GenerateDataKey), principal, timestamp
Retention and legal hold:
- Audit/forensic logs retention: default 7 years (customer legal requires FINRA-like), immutable S3 archive with object lock for retention periods
- Hot telemetry (operational traces/metrics): 90 days in splunk/datadog for triage; then summary aggregates moved to cold storage
- Log deletion: must support legal hold overrides and export prior to deletion
KMS & encryption:
- Customer-managed CMK required for data-at-rest (logs and model artifacts). AWS KMS CMK ARN to be supplied; bring-your-own-key (BYOK) supported
- Envelope encryption: runtime uses platform key to encrypt payload; customer key used for wrapping. Support for CloudHSM-backed keys discussed for HSM requirement
- Audit of key rotation: provide key rotation events to SIEM (who rotated, previous key id, effective time)
SIEM ingestion details requested by Verdigris team:
- Splunk: HEC token-based, batched events, recommended batch size 1000 events or 5MB, backpressure behavior documented
- Syslog: RFC5424 with structured-data block containing JSON payload
- S3 export: hourly/near-real-time partitioned by date/tenant, gzipped JSONL, server-side encryption with CMK, object lock metadata for retention
Schema/Versioning and change control:
- Provide versioned log-schema artifacts (semantic versioning). Breaking change policy: 30 days notice + parallel fields for 90 days
- Mapping doc required for Splunk sourcetypes and field extractions (deliverable requested)
Operational controls and access:
- RBAC for log access: only security + designated SMEs can see full tenant identifiers; product support sees pseudonymized ids
- Audit of who accessed logs (time, principal, justification) must be exported to SIEM
